works.title: The Agricola
works.source: Tacitus, Agricola & Germania (Oxford translation, 1877) · Project Gutenberg #7524 · public domain
works.note: His life of his father-in-law, the governor of Britain — and the source of the chieftain Calgacus's verdict on Rome: “they make a desert and call it peace.”

works.title: The Germania
works.source: Tacitus, Agricola & Germania (Oxford translation, 1877) · Project Gutenberg #7524 · public domain
works.note: His ethnography of the tribes beyond the Rhine — Rome's mirror held up to the people it called barbarian.

works.title: The Histories — The Opening
works.source: Tacitus, The Histories (trans. W. Hamilton Fyfe, 1912) · Project Gutenberg #16927 · public domain
works.note: His statement of method — to write “without partiality and without hatred” — and the grim catalogue of the age he set out to record.

works.title: The Histories — The Verdict on Galba
works.source: Tacitus, The Histories (trans. W. Hamilton Fyfe, 1912) · Project Gutenberg #16927 · public domain
works.note: The squalid end of the emperor Galba and Tacitus's famous epitaph: all would have judged him fit to rule, had he never ruled.

works.title: The Annals, Books I–VI (the reign of Tiberius)
works.note: The surviving early Annals, in an older translation.
